title: Games page: tabs, headed sections with true counts, status bar, virtual grid
covers: Games page layout, tabs, counts, search and filters
context: The Games page has the tabs All, Installed, Built-in, Archipelia ready, Archipelago index and Updates. All shows the headed sections Installed, Built-in, Archipelia ready and Archipelago index, each with a true count. The status bar adds up the same worlds. The grid draws only the cards in view and its scrollbar sits in its own gutter.
changed: views/GameStore: new source names (Built-in, Archipelia ready, Archipelago index), sections, tabs and the Source and Verified filters
Cards show no hover hints; the details dialog replaces them

setup.label: launch
setup.text: The bundle-4 launch above. If the welcome tour opens by itself, press Skip.

setup.label: network
setup.text: Needed. The catalog index and the Archipelia ready list come from the network.

setup.label: engine
setup.text: Ready (the Engine page under App shows Ready).

setup.label: window
setup.text: A normal window, about 1250 pixels wide or more, so several cards fit in a row.

steps: Launch with the command of this test. In the sidebar, under Library, press Games. The page opens on All. The tabs in the page header run All, Installed, Built-in, Archipelia ready, Archipelago index, Updates.

On All read the section headings from the top: Installed, Built-in, Archipelia ready, Archipelago index. Each has a number badge. With nothing installed, Installed reads No game installed yet and keeps its heading.
Read the status bar at the bottom: All worlds, Ins Updates shows only when a game can be updated, and No release yet only when some world has no releas The four heading counts add up to All worlds.
Scroll the list to the end. The scrollbar sits in its own strip and never covers a card. No line reading Showing x of y appears. Hover a card for two seconds: no tooltip hint shows.

Press each tab. Installed, Built-in, Archipelia ready and Archipelago index each show one heading with its own count. Updates shows cards with the status Update, or the text Every installed game is up to date. Return to All.
Type a game name in Search worlds The sections narrow together, empty ones vanish, and All worlds reads Search a nonsense word: No world matches shows Search Relic of the Pas Clear the search.
Press Add filter, pick Source, then Archipelago index. The list narrows across the sections. Press Clear filters. Add the filter Verified, then clear it again.

Press the Refresh index button next to the search box: it spins, then stops, with no red message. Press Add from file in the status bar: a picker for .apworld files opens. Cancel it. Nothing is added.
pass: The six tabs exist and each lists the right worlds. All shows Installed, Built-in, Archipelia ready, Archipelago index in that order, each with a count badge.
The four heading counts add up to All worlds in the status bar.
No Showing x of y line and no hover hints. The scrollbar has its own gutter and the long list scrolls smoothly.
Search and filters narrow the list and All worlds reads x of y. Relic of the Past sits once, under Archipelia ready, with Verified.
fail: A tab or a section is missing or out of order, or a heading count does not match the cards under it or the status bar.
A Showing x of y line shows, a hover hint shows on a card, or the scrollbar covers the cards.
The list stutters badly while scrolling, or the page freezes for seconds when it opens.
Search or filters skip a section, or Refresh index or Add from file shows a red error although the network is fine.
notes: Card details, Add and Remove progress and the search jump are in the test Games cards. Worlds found by topic are in the test Archipelia ready: found by topic.
A game only shows Update when a newer world release exists. The Updates tab may well be empty today, which is not a failure.
When GitHub returned more Archipelia ready worlds than the page shows, a line reads Showing the N most recently updated of M Archipelia ready worlds. That is correct.
Descriptions and art need the network. Without it the cards stay plain, which is not a failure. Say in your note whether the page still lags.
